summary: Patrick R. Uhlmann is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he studied under Robert Buswell (attested 2012).

Patrul Rinpoche (1808–1887) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jigme Gyelwai Nyugu and Zhabkar Tsokdruk Rangdrol, and taught figures such as Zhenphen Chökyi Nangwa and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Educated at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell Universities (PhD ~1994), she taught at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016) and served as assistant curator at the Asian Art Museum (1997–2002).
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and Emory University (attested 1998).

Paul B. Donnelly is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and also studied under Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe and Lobsang Gyatso. He holds a post at Northern Arizona University.

Paul Carus (1852–1919) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Tübingen. He worked for the Open Court Publishing Company and edited The Monist and The Open Court from around 1887/1890 to 1919.

Paul Copp is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Princeton University (PhD attested 2005 under Stephen F. Teiser), later holding posts at Western Michigan University and the University of Chicago.

Paul Crowe is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He was a graduate student at the University of Calgary, where he studied under Leslie S. Kawamura and Daniel L. Overmyer, and became a professor at Simon Fraser University (attested 2010).

Paul David Devanandan (1901–1962) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Presidency College, Chennai, and Yale University. He served as professor at United Theological College, Bangalore (1932–1949), and became director of the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society in 1956.

Paul David Numrich is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan in 1992. His posts include appointments at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus (both attested 2006).

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Union (1955), and also founded Wissen und Wandel (1955).

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1945–1957) and Collège de France (1946–1964), and directed Hōbōgirin (~1927–1979).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the universities of Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, learning under Christian Lassen. He held posts at the University of Geneva, RWTH Aachen, and University of Berlin, before becoming professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh (~1976–2023) and also served as head of the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed his doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held posts at Michigan State University (attested 1992) and the University of Rochester (attested 2000).
Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1955–1958). He held a post at the University of California, San Francisco, from around 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter (born 1939) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1968–1972), and held a post at Union Theological Seminary (~2007–2017).

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Liège. He served as a professor at Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University (from 1883), where he became rector in 1919.
Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Rupert Gethin and also studied under Paul Dundas.

Paul G. Hackett is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Columbia University. He served as Tibetan collection curator at the University of Virginia and later held research and lecturing posts in Tibetan at Columbia University.
